what: The research series for XAUUSD — the 50,000-bar corpus this program was originally researched and certified on. It is NOT the market the funded EA trades.
was: data/forex/xauusd/XAUUSD_{M15,H1,D1}.csv (the data of record until 2026-09-21), then archive/frozen_corpus/ for one commit
now: deleted from the working tree. `midas_sweep.frozen_bars()` is the only reader; it verifies these pins and refuses anything that does not match, which is what makes a restore checkable rather than hopeful.
superseded_by: data/forex/xauusd/XAUUSD_{M15,H1,D1}_upcomers.csv — the terminal's own history for account 1428765, i.e. the bars the EA actually trades
superseded_by_note: Fetched with `scripts/midas_fetch_history.py --suffix _upcomers`. Its own XAUUSD history BEGINS 2026-01-12 11:15 UTC, which is why 7,752 bars of the frozen `wf` window exist only in the deleted series and no EA side can be compared there.
why_retired: Two series both answered to "the gold bars". Inside the tick-covered window they disagreed about 21 bars, and about the units of their spread column (this one's raw `spread` is DOLLARS, the venue's is POINTS).

That ambiguity is not cosmetic: a staged spread file from the wrong series handed the EA a flat $0.15 half-spread where the engine of record charged $0.42 — a constant $0.135 per fill that moved a long's stop $0.136 further out, so the market ground through the two levels 105 minutes apart.
One divergence was misread as a +120-minute clock fault for a day, because the first divergent trade closed exactly 7,200 s apart on a trade whose entry agreed to the second.
why_deleted: The only reason to keep the bytes was that the certified arithmetic was computed on them. That reason was real — but its price was central evidence that nobody without a copy can re-check, on a series no fetch can reproduce.

The operator's call on 2026-09-21: delete the copy, re-point the regression law at the series that still exists, and record exactly what stops being checkable (below) rather than leaving an unfalsifiable citation in place.
The pins stay. A restore from `248db66` is verified by SHA-256 against this manifest, so 'the numbers moved' and 'the bytes moved' cannot be confused.
what_it_is_not: Not a market. See the measured disagreement below.
Not the same units as the venue's series — dollars vs points.
Not true UTC in the same sense: this one was stamped in true UTC, the venue's is server wall clock and needs the pinned offset in configs/mt5/server_offsets.json.
Not something any default may reach — the loader names its own path and there is no fallback.

measured_disagreement.window: tick-covered 2026-09-04 .. 2026-09-16, at the venue's asserted +120 min
measured_disagreement.note: The 3 are 2026-09-07 17:45/18:00/18:15; the 18 include 2026-09-07 22:00-23:45 and 2026-09-16 22:00-23:45. Measured while both series existed; re-runnable only after a restore.

citations_that_stop_being_checkable: tests/test_midas_minlot_veto.py — the n=151 / +1.474R regression law (the veto never fires on the certified corpus). RE-POINTED: the same claim is now pinned on the venue's own bars, n=53 / +14.256R over 2026-01-12..03-31, vetoed=0 (measured 2026-09-21).

artifacts/midas_sweep_20260917.json — the sweep artifact scripts/midas_parity.py reads as SWEEP_ANCHOR (its REVERSE_DIRECTION/wf entry is n=151 / net_r +1.474). It cannot be regenerated: scripts/midas_sweep.py:main reads the deleted series and now refuses. `anchor_match()` therefore can never be satisfied again; it already reports NO-ANCHOR on every venue-corpus window.

scripts/midas_sweep.py:main and scripts/midas_variant_research.py — their outputs are no longer producible on this checkout at all. Both refuse with the restore instructions instead of silently running on the venue's bars.

scripts/midas_parity.py --window wf --corpus frozen and --window oos --corpus frozen — the two windows that declared this corpus. They were already unrunnable (the venue cannot serve their spans); with the series deleted they are unrunnable without a restore by construction. The refusal is the intended behaviour, not a fault.

docs/MIDASTOUCH_PROTOCOL.md §1 (the original data of record), §10 (amendment 2: 151 trades / +1.47R), §15 (n=151 / +1.474R, vetoed=0) — the certified arithmetic. As history these citations remain true and their corpus is named; they can no longer be re-derived.
docs/MIDASTOUCH_V2_REGISTER.md — 'python 151 tr / +1.474R vs EA 151 tr / +1.478R, max|dR| 0.0005' and the n=151 line in the certificate summary.
docs/MIDASTOUCH_CLOSEOUT_20260917.md and docs/MIDASTOUCH_CLOSEOUT_20260919.md — Certificate 1 (WF) 'PASS, 151 vs 151 keyed trades' and 'the sweep anchor reproduced exactly'.
docs/DATA_SCOPE_AND_CLOCK_20260920.md — the parity comparison table's python leg '151tr +1.474R'.

docs/PARITY_VETO_AND_CORPUS_20260921.md — the 21-bar disagreement between the two series is the measurement that justified the retirement, and it is now a record rather than a reproducible check (its counts are pinned above).

docs/PARITY_ENTRY_SIGNALS_20260921.md §5c — '32 of 32 sweep anchors reproduce exactly ... REVERSE_DIRECTION/wf = 151 trades, +1.474R'. That reproduction was measured while the bytes existed; it cannot be repeated without a restore.

docs/GOLD_ARMING_DECISION_20260921.md — the certified-window row of the power table (n=151, +0.0098R/trade, sd 1.082). Its conclusion stands as a recorded measurement, but the sample can no longer be re-derived from a checkout.
docs/FROZEN_CORPUS_20260921.md — the retirement record itself; §5 now carries the restore path.

tests/test_parity_corpus.py — the byte-level corpus-disagreement tests skip unless the series is restored (with the restore command in the skip message). The hash-pin and deletion-record tests do NOT skip: they build their own fixture, so the mechanism stays tested with the bytes gone.
not_affected_note: NOT gold_wfo / GOLD_WFO_VERDICT. artifacts/gold_wfo.json and docs/GOLD_WFO_VERDICT_20260919.md are produced by scripts/gold_walkforward.py, which loads bars from the terminal at run time (mt5_data.load_m5), so the walk-forward verdict (fold-mean t = +0.52 over the venue's span, 16,278 bars from 2026-01-12) is a VENUE-corpus number and never depended on this series. The same is true of the news stand-down measurements (docs/GOLD_NEWS_SENSITIVITY_20260921.md, docs/GOLD_NEWS_WIDTH_20260921.md): their harness imports gold_walkforward/mt5_data, not this corpus. Naming a non-dependency explicitly is the point — the first draft of the retirement doc inferred the opposite and had to be corrected.

restore.then: set status back to 'kept' here, and run `python -m pytest tests/test_parity_corpus.py -q`: the hash of every file is verified against the pins below, so a partial or edited restore fails loudly.
restore.caveat: Restoring makes the old numbers re-checkable again; it does not make them current. The data of record stays the venue's own series.
